Bacillus cereus in reconstituted infant milk: statistical analysis

Analysis of B. cereus counts (vegetative cells and spores) in reconstituted infant milk, comparing two reconstitution methods (FDA, WHO) over time at three storage temperatures. The analysis is delivered as an R Markdown report.

Study design

  • Outcomes: log10 counts of vegetative cells and of spores (already log-transformed in the data file).
  • Factors: Time (0, 6, 24, 30, 36, 48, 54, 72 h), Treatment (FDA, WHO), Temperature (4, 10, 20 °C).
  • Replication: 3 replicates per combination (balanced: 8 × 2 × 3 cells, 144 observations per outcome).
  • Time 0 is a single baseline measurement shared by all temperatures (copied to each temperature in the data).
  • Independence: three independent milk samples were prepared; a separate tube was used for each time point and temperature. Tubes are therefore neither fully independent nor repeated measures on the same unit. All p-values should be read as indicative.

Data

Cereous.xlsx, one sheet per outcome (first row is a title row, the table starts in row 2):

Sheet Outcome
Forme vegetative vegetative cells
Spore spores

Long format, one row per observation: Time, Treatment, Temperature, followed by the log10 count in the fourth column.

Analysis

  1. Exploratory plots: time courses, change from time 0, difference between methods.
  2. Three-way ANOVA (Time × Treatment × Temperature, type III sums of squares, sum-to-zero contrasts), fitted because it was requested in the review. Holm correction over the 7 terms. Every term contains Time or Temperature, so one large effect (growth at 20 °C) makes almost every term significant.
  3. Diagnostics: residual normality (Q–Q plots, Shapiro–Wilk) and equality of variances (pooled within-cell SD by temperature).
  4. Main analysis, stratified by temperature: two-way ANOVA (Time × Treatment) within each temperature, with its own error variance (32 residual df). Holm correction over the 9 tests per outcome. Follow-up contrasts with emmeans:
    • effect of time within each treatment (Holm over 6 tests);
    • Dunnett comparison of each time against time 0, within temperature and treatment;
    • WHO − FDA at each time (Holm over 24 comparisons per outcome).
  5. Appendix: sensitivity of the treatment effect to the time-0 baseline (models with and without time 0).

Conclusions Summary and limitations

Main results

  • Growth occurs essentially only at 20 °C: vegetative cells increase by about 6.5 log10 within 48 h; spores increase only at 72 h (about +2.5 log10).
  • At 20 °C the WHO method gives faster growth of vegetative cells between 6 and 36 h; both reach the same plateau.
  • At 4 and 10 °C no change over time was detected. For spores WHO is lower than FDA at all time points (about −0.25 log10 at 4 °C and −0.44 log10 at 10 °C); the offset is already present at time 0.

Limitations

  • Tubes drawn from the same milk sample are not independent, and there are only three replicates per cell.
  • Residuals for spores are not normal, and their variance is larger at 20 °C (pooled SD 0.42 vs about 0.20).
  • A non-significant result does not show equivalence.
  • Several findings are borderline (for example the spore difference at 30 h and 20 °C) and should be confirmed on more data.
